First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(2\cdot {5}^{x})=2\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{5}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the graph of $y={5}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943873/assets/02d46e13c84fc575f489a9870f3b1213eb3d180f3f5ef6e6a546d3acfe4b2282.png)

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound  as $x$ increases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{5}^{x}=\infty .
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
2\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{5}^{x}=2\cdot \infty =\infty .
$$
